main_text.head: Caput. 9.
main_text.p: NOnum caput vnico argumento, eoque ab ipsius Pauli libertati suæ in aliorum gratiam renuntiantis exemplo, sumpto idololatricas illas comessationes hominum saluti plurimum officientes dissuadet: Nam quod Paulus in Corinthiorum, hoc Corinthios in fratrum gratiam facere æquum est. Duplicem libertatis suæ renuntiationem proponit, vnam particularem, qua à debito stipendio ab ecclesijs exigendo abstinuit. De hac agitur vsq; ad vers. 19. alteram generalem, qua omnes suas actiones, ad hanc non suæ libertatis sed alienæ salutis normam exigit. In reliquo capite in priore parte duo ostendit, primùm se optimo iure aliquam & quidem satis amplam laboris sui mercedem capere potuisse vsque ad vers. 15. Secundò se hoc non fecisse vers. 15.16.17.18. ius probatur hoc argumento, Apostolis vtpote primariis euangelij ministris, iustum stipendium exigere licet: At Ego sum Apostolus. Assumptio, quæ priore loco proponitur, in primis verbis occurrit duobus argumentis stabilita: vna à causa efficiente & formali apostolatus, immediata ipsius Dei vocatione

page.notes: The first letter N is a large woodcut initial joined to "Onum". The text continues beyond the bottom of this part. Some words in the first line are printed with spacing irregularities; "Paulus in Corinthiorum" appears to omit a word (the printed text reads as shown). Part 2 of a page; the upper part is cut off. The catchword and signature are as printed; "cationē" is partly obscured. The final word may be "vocatione" with the -ne partly lost; read as "vocatione" in the line "vo-" / "cationes" at the foot.
